newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire bans demos, troops to fire on looters.
newsitem.headline: Zaire bans demos, troops to fire on looters.

text.p: Zaire on Monday banned demonstrations and authorised troops to open fire on anyone caught looting or engaging in vandalism, the government said.

A statement issued after a special cabinet meeting said the measures had become necessary because of attacks on Rwandans and Burundians in Zaire following a Tutsi revolt in the east. Zaire accuses Rwandan troops of fighting alongside the rebels.
Protests had been planned in Kinshasa for Tuesday.
Demonstrators last week called on part-Tutsi Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo to resign and attacked homes and businesses belonging to Tutsis in the Zaire capital.
"Our country having been unjustly attacked by these two countries (Rwanda and Burundi), it is understandable that our people should feel xenophobic sentiments," the statement said.
The demonstration ban was indefinite and applied to all Zaire. Kinshasa security patrols would be strengthened, it said.
Anti-Tutsi sentiment has risen. Hundreds of frightened Tutsis have fled to neighbouring Congo or gone into hiding.
Tutsis were attacked or harassed during protests in Kinshasa last week. Many Tutsi families have reported missing relatives.
About 400 Banyamulenge Tutsis in dugout canoes escaped into Congo on Monday, joining some 200 others who have crossed the Zaire River into the capital Brazzaville in the past two weeks.

They would have had to sneak through unguarded crossing points or bribe their way through. "If we try to get out by the official channels we get stopped at the border and accused of being the enemy," said one Tutsi in hiding in Kinshasa.
